text:
Maya Chen: Heads-up — product asked for a new UX: when an embed request is too big, instead of just 413 we should either return a smarter hint header or auto-accept and queue an async split job. tradeoffs?
Kevin Patel: +1 to hint header. Auto-splitting has storage/latency implications. we already have splitters in runtime but making it async changes SLOs.
Amanda R: Curious what "smarter hint" would include. dims? bytes? sample of offending items so SDK can retry cheap?
Maya Chen: idea: 413 + header `X-Embed-Reject-Info: dims=16,oversize-bytes=23400,suggested-split=3` so clients can decide. Also console can surface a 'why rejected' card.
Oliver: I worry about client fragmentation. some SDKs won't implement retry logic. fallback UX could be server-side: accept small single-file autosplit for simple cases, else 413+hint for big ones.
Sasha: telemetry-wise we need to tag the rejection path. propose adding `routing_class=reject_hint` and `split_strategy=server_async|client_retry|server_inline` to traces/metrics.
Kevin Patel: +1 to telemetry tags. Also add a new dashboard panel: embed-routing -> "reject vs autosplit ratio" and heatmap for payload bytes vs dims.
Amanda R: For console, a small control to toggle server_inline for low-risk tenants might help. feature-flag rollout only.
Maya Chen: rollout plan suggestion: feature-flag `embed_autosplit_inline` default off. enable 5% tenants for 1 day, check latency and disk IO. then 20%, 50% etc. if regressions, auto-revert.
Oliver: Can we make autosplit synchronous only when number_of_items < 50 and avg_dim uniform? avoids huge re-encodes.
Kevin Patel: yes. runtime can check `len(req.vecs) < 50 && dims_uniform` before inline split. otherwise return hint.
Sasha: metric list I want: embed.reject.count, embed.autosplit.inline.count, embed.autosplit.async.queue_len, embed.client_retry.rate, embed.latency.P95_by_path. Also tag by tenant_id+route.
Amanda R: UX ask: add a small sample payload viewer in the rejection card so support can repro quickly. link to traces.
Maya Chen: example of suggested response headers we discussed:

```
HTTP/1.1 413 Payload Too Large
Content-Type: application/json
X-Embed-Reject-Info: dims=1536;max_per_item=8192;oversize_by_bytes=34210;suggested_split=4
X-Embed-Routing-Class: reject_hint
```

Kevin Patel: love the header shape. make `suggested_split` optional when we can't estimate.
Oliver: one API debate: should we accept mixed-dim payloads and normalize on server (up/down-sample) vs reject? normalizing can hide rough client bugs though.
Sasha: if we normalize, telemetry must record `normalization=up|down|none` and we should sample outputs for QA. privacy concerns though.
Amanda R: also consider cost — sampling and re-embedding on server adds GPU cycles. need a cost estimate per 1k requests when normalization enabled.
Maya Chen: Ops: if inline autosplit writes tmp files, ensure cleanup on failures. add a small e2e test for leak scenarios.
Kevin Patel: Implementation tasks: 1) Add header format and server-side 413 path (eng-runtime), 2) telemetry tags & metrics (eng-platform/observability), 3) console card + heatmap (console team), 4) feature flag and rollout playbook (releases).
Oliver: PR note — I'll add `dims_uniform` helper and a cheap estimator for `suggested_split` (by bytes/dim). Will post bench numbers.
deploy-bot: canary deploy of embed-routing-v2 scheduled to prod-canary at 1749990000 :rocket:
Sasha: rollout checklist: create dashboard with alert when embed.autosplit.inline.count spikes >10x baseline, add runbook link, and sample traces retention for 48h.
Amanda R: final UX nit: error message copy should say "Try batching smaller items or enable client-side split; see console for hints" — short and actionable.
Maya Chen: ok I'll draft the console card mock, upload to design channel, and follow up with estimated telemetry dimensions. thanks all :thumbsup:
